parameters.description: Optional starting line number (1-indexed). If provided, returns content from this line to the end of the page.

tools.description: Fetch text content from a website URL. If a regex pattern is provided, returns matching lines with line numbers and surrounding context. If no pattern is provided, returns the full page content.

parameters.description: The URL of the webpage to open.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Optional regular expression pattern to search for in the page content. Use standard regex syntax. Search is case-insensitive. If not provided, returns the full page content.

parameters.name: max_matches
parameters.description: Maximum number of matches to return. Defaults to 50.

parameters.name: context_lines
parameters.description: Number of context lines to show before and after each match. Defaults to 10.

parameters.name: image_url
parameters.description: The URL of the image to view.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: This action searches the web. You can use search operators like site:reddit.com when needed. Set include_image to attach each result's main image when the page has one. Set image_only to return only those main images. Use image_only when the user wants pictures instead of a separate image search. Image results are saved under the sandbox artifacts searched_images directory and the returned file path can be passed to later tools such as edit_image and render_file.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The search query to look up on the web. Search operators like site:reddit.com are allowed.

parameters.name: num_results
parameters.description: The number of results to return. Optional, default 10, max 30. When image_only is true, this is how many images to return.

parameters.name: include_image
parameters.description: When true, attach each result's main image (og:image, twitter:image, or YouTube thumbnail) when the page has one. Pages without an image are still returned. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: image_only
parameters.description: When true, return only pages that have a main image, as images, and drop the rest. Use this when the user wants pictures. It replaces a separate image search tool and implies include_image.

tools.name: x_keyword_search
tools.description: Advanced search tool for X Posts.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description:
The search query string for X advanced search. Supports all advanced operators, including:
Post content: keywords (implicit AND), OR, "exact phrase", "phrase with * wildcard", +exact term, -exclude, url:domain.
From/to/mentions: from:user, to:user, @user, list:id or list:slug.
Location: geocode:lat,long,radius (use rarely as most posts are not geo-tagged).
Time/ID: since:YYYY-MM-DD, until:YYYY-MM-DD, since:YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS_TZ, until:YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS_TZ, since_time:unix, until_time:unix, since_id:id, max_id:id, within_time:Xd/Xh/Xm/Xs.
Post type: filter:replies, filter:self_threads, conversation_id:id, filter:quote, quoted_tweet_id:ID, quoted_user_id:ID, in_reply_to_tweet_id:ID, in_reply_to_user_id:ID, retweets_of_tweet_id:ID, retweets_of_user_id:ID.
Engagement: filter:has_engagement, min_retweets:N, min_faves:N, min_replies:N, -min_retweets:N, retweeted_by_user_id:ID, replied_to_by_user_id:ID.
Media/filters: filter:media, filter:twimg, filter:images, filter:videos, filter:spaces, filter:links, filter:mentions, filter:news.
Most filters can be negated with -. Use parentheses for grouping. Spaces mean AND; OR must be uppercase.

Example query:
(puppy OR kitten) (sweet OR cute) filter:images min_faves:10

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of posts to return. Default to 3, max is 10.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Sort by Top or Latest. The default is Top. You must output the mode with a capital first letter.

tools.name: create_image
tools.description:
Create an image with Grok Imagine and show it to the user. Use this whenever the user asks for an image to be generated, drawn, designed, edited, restyled or changed — including requests like "make it wider", "remove the background", "turn this photo into a poster". `create_image` is a tool: make the image with a function call. It is not a render component or XML element, and written as one in your response it makes nothing.

The image streams into the conversation while it renders, so by the time this returns the user has already seen it. Do not attach the same image again with another tool; write one or two sentences about it instead.

To edit or combine existing pictures, pass 1 to 4 of them in `images`. Each entry is a file path from an earlier result or an attachment, or an image id from earlier in this conversation. One entry edits that picture; two to four combine them, with the first as the base. If an edit needs more than 4 images, first combine the input images into a 2x2 grid and pass that.

The result gives you the image id and, when this conversation has a workspace, the saved file path. Use the path from code execution or the shell; use the id to edit this image again or to animate it.

Set `display` to false only when the image is an intermediate step the user should not see yet — a frame you are about to animate, an asset you are about to composite. The default is true.

One call makes one image; for several images make several calls with different prompts. Never create a named real person from a text prompt alone — start from a photo the user supplied or one you found, and pass it in `images`.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: Prompt for the image generation model: a lossless description of what the user asked for. Keep every detail the user specified and add no subjects, styles, or details they did not specify. The prompt must not present incorrect information. Do not generate images promoting hate speech or violence.

parameters.name: images
parameters.description: Pictures to edit or combine, 1 to 4. Each entry is a file path from an earlier result or an attachment, or an image id from earlier in this conversation. One entry edits that picture; two to four combine them, with the first as the base. If an edit needs more than 4 images, first combine the input images into a 2x2 grid and pass that. Leave it out to create a new image from the prompt.

parameters.name: aspect_ratio
parameters.description: Aspect ratio of the image, chosen from the user's request: 2:3 for vertical (portraits, posters), 1:1 for square (icons, profiles), 16:9 for wide (landscapes, cinematic), 9:16 for tall (phone wallpapers, stories), 3:2 for horizontal photos. "auto" lets the image model choose the framing from the prompt. Defaults to auto. When editing, auto keeps the first picture's aspect ratio.

parameters.name: display
parameters.description: Whether the user sees the image as it renders. Defaults to true. Set it to false only for an intermediate step the user should not see yet.

tools.name: create_video
tools.description:
Create a short video with Grok Imagine and save it as a file. Use this whenever the user asks for a video, animation or clip. `create_video` is a tool: make the video with a function call. It is not a render component or XML element, and written as one in your response it makes nothing.

This tool does not show the video to the user. After the call returns, attach the saved file with the `render_file` component, using the returned path, in your final response, and write one or two sentences about it. Rendering can take minutes and is charged per clip: make one call per video the user asked for, and do not retry a failed call unless the user asks.

`prompt` is always required: describe subject, motion, camera and mood. The other inputs select the mode:
- Text to video: `prompt` only.
- Image to video: `image`. It becomes the first frame and the clip keeps its aspect ratio; `prompt` says how it moves.
- First and last frame: `last_frame`, with or without `image`. The clip ends exactly on it; the same picture for both makes a loop.
- Keyframes: up to 4, each a picture and the second it must appear at, at least 1/3 s from each other, from the start and from the end.
- References: up to 14 `reference_images` of people, objects, clothing or settings. They are re-rendered, not used as frames. Cite them in the prompt as `<IMAGE_0>`, `<IMAGE_1>`, … in list order.

Every picture is a file path from an earlier result or an attachment, or an image id from earlier in this conversation. One call takes at most 14 pictures.

Set `duration`, `aspect_ratio` and `resolution` only when the user asks. `1080p` works only for text to video and image to video.

Never create a named real person from a text prompt alone — start from a photo the user supplied or one you found.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: Prompt for the video model: subject, motion, camera and mood. With `image`, say how the picture moves. Cite reference images as `<IMAGE_0>`, `<IMAGE_1>`, … in list order. Stay faithful to what the user asked for.

parameters.name: image
parameters.description: Picture the clip starts on: it becomes the exact first frame. A file path from an earlier result or an attachment, or an image id from earlier in this conversation. On its own it makes an image-to-video clip that keeps the picture's aspect ratio.

parameters.name: last_frame
parameters.description: Picture the clip ends exactly on. A file path from an earlier result or an attachment, or an image id from earlier in this conversation. Give the same picture as `image` to make a loop.

parameters.name: keyframes
parameters.description: Pictures that must appear at given moments, up to 4. Each entry has an `image` and the `timestamp_s` it appears at, at least 1/3 s from each other, from the start and from the end of the clip.

parameters.name: reference_images
parameters.description: Pictures of people, objects, clothing or settings the video should include, up to 14. They are re-rendered, not used as frames. Each entry is a file path from an earlier result or an attachment, or an image id from earlier in this conversation. Cite them in the prompt as `<IMAGE_0>`, `<IMAGE_1>`, … in list order.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: Length of the clip in whole seconds, 1 to 15. Defaults to 6. Set it only when the user asks.

parameters.name: aspect_ratio
parameters.description: Aspect ratio of the clip: 16:9 for wide, 9:16 for tall, 1:1 for square, 4:3 and 3:4 for standard, 3:2 and 2:3 for photo shapes. Set it only when the user asks. It is ignored with `image` alone, which keeps the picture's own ratio.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Resolution of the clip. Defaults to 480p. Set it only when the user asks. 1080p works only for text to video and image to video.

tools.name: search_connected_tools
tools.description: Search the user's connected services for available tools. The user has these services connected: Voice (generate spoken audio from text), Automations (schedule a prompt for Grok to run later, once or on a repeating cadence). Only use this for the user's connected services — not for your built-in tools which you can call directly. Call this when the user needs to interact with any of these services. Describe the ACTION you need (e.g., 'search pages', 'send message', 'create issue', 'list files'). Returns ranked results with full argument schemas so you can call_connected_tool immediately. If the user needs a service that is not connected, call list_available_connectors. If it returns names, pass the one to three this ask needs to request_connector_auth; do not invent names. If the list is empty, use the name the user said or the name from an auth error.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Describe the action to perform using keywords that match tool names and descriptions. Good examples: 'search pages', 'create issue', 'send message', 'list files', 'read email', 'calendar events', 'query database'. Bad examples: 'what tools are available', 'my connected apps', 'list integrations'.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of tools to return (default: 10, max: 20). Use a higher limit when exploring available capabilities.

tools.name: call_connected_tool
tools.description: Execute a connected tool by name with JSON arguments. Only for tools discovered via search_connected_tools — not for your built-in tools. Always use search_connected_tools first to find the right tool and get its argument schema. Pass the tool name exactly as returned by search_connected_tools.

parameters.name: tool_name
parameters.description: The exact tool name as returned by search_connected_tools results.

parameters.name: arguments
parameters.description: JSON object containing the arguments to pass to the tool. Check the input_schema from search results.

tools.name: list_available_connectors
tools.description: List services the user can connect but has not connected yet. Call this when search_connected_tools finds nothing for a service the user asked about, before request_connector_auth. Returns display names to pass to request_connector_auth. Do not invent names that are not in the result.

tools.name: weather_forecast
tools.description:
Fetch the weather for a location: current conditions, a daily forecast up to 10 days ahead, and hourly detail for a chosen day.
- Use this for questions about weather, temperature, rain, snow, wind, humidity, sunrise or sunset at a place.
- Pass specific_date when the user asks about one day (today, tomorrow, a weekday, a date); omit it for a multi-day outlook.
- For weather where the user is (no place named), omit location and pass the user's latitude and longitude. Take them from a device Location line in User Info if there is one; otherwise, if get_device_location is available, call it first with importance "recommended". If you get no coordinates, pass the user's approximate city as location and say that is the place you used.
- The result includes a card_id. Call render_card with it only when the user asked about the weather. When the weather only informs a broader request (planning a day or trip, what to wear, an event), mention the relevant conditions in a sentence and skip the card.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: The city or place to get weather for, e.g. "New York", "London", "Tokyo", "San Francisco, CA". Include the state or country when the name alone is ambiguous. Omit for the user's current location.

parameters.name: latitude
parameters.description: The user's latitude in decimal degrees, from get_device_location or a device Location line. Only for weather where the user is; pass with longitude.

parameters.name: longitude
parameters.description: The user's longitude in decimal degrees. Pass with latitude.

parameters.name: focus
parameters.description: What the user is asking about: "precipitation" for rain questions ("will it rain tonight?"), "snowfall" for snow questions, "none" for general weather.

parameters.name: specific_date
parameters.description: Day to get detailed hourly weather for: "today" (also for tonight, this evening, current conditions), "tomorrow", a weekday name such as "friday" or "next monday", or a date like "2026-09-20". Omit (or pass "none") for a multi-day forecast.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Temperature unit for the result and card. Pass "celsius" or "fahrenheit" only when the user names a unit ("in celsius", "in °F"); otherwise leave "auto" to use the user's locale.

tools.name: sports_search
tools.description: Live and current-season sports data from X: scores, box scores, team records, standings, schedules, player profiles, and stat leaders. Use it for a specific team, player, game, date, or round in a listed league; not for other leagues or past seasons. Results include a card_id; pass it to render_card to show a sports card.

parameters.name: league
parameters.description: Soccer: epl (Premier League), laliga, seriea, bundesliga, ligue1.

parameters.name: request
parameters.description:
- team: record, standing, recent and upcoming games (needs `team`)
- player: profile and recent performances (needs `player`; `team` disambiguates)
- event: one game's score and details (needs `team`; pick with `event`, `date`, or `opponent`)
- schedule: a team's season (needs `team`; NFL `round` narrows), or all games on a `date` or in a `round`. With none, the current NFL week or soccer matchweek, or today's NBA/MLB/NHL games
- standings: the table (`team` highlights one)
- leaders: season stat leaders; NFL `round` gives one week's

parameters.name: team
parameters.description: One team as the user named it ("Kansas City Chiefs", "Chiefs", "KC"). Exactly one team; "New York" is ambiguous.

parameters.name: opponent
parameters.description: For `event`: the other team ("Chiefs vs Bills" → team: Chiefs, opponent: Bills).

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: For `player`: full name ("Patrick Mahomes").

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: For `event`: last completed, next scheduled, or live. Omit for live if in progress, else last.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: YYYY-MM-DD, US Eastern. For `event`: the team's game that day (overrides `event`). For `schedule` without `team`: every game that day.

parameters.name: round
parameters.description: NFL week or soccer matchweek, for `schedule` (default current) and NFL `leaders` (default season). NBA/MLB/NHL use `date`.

tools.name: request_connector_auth
tools.description:
Show the user an in-chat card to connect or reauthenticate one or more connectors (at most 3). Call this only when the current user request cannot be completed without those connectors, and for each one either: (1) the user has never connected it, or (2) a connected-tool or search_connected_tools result says auth expired or needs re-authentication.
Do not call speculatively, "just in case", or for a connector that already worked this turn. Do not call more than once per connector per turn. Pass only names this ask needs, at most 3, never the full catalog.
If search finds nothing, call list_available_connectors and pass one to three of its names. If that list is empty, pass the user's or auth-error name as a one-element list.
After the result, for each connected name call search_connected_tools for the original task and then call_connected_tool. If search finds nothing, tell the user the connector is not ready yet — do not invent a workaround unless they ask.
On skipped / timeout / unavailable, continue without those connectors. Do not work around them unless they ask.
Success is {"results":[{"status":"connected"|"skipped","connector":"<id>"},...]}. On denial or failure of the whole card: {"error":"permission_denied"|"unavailable"|"user_cancelled"|"unknown_connector"}. The server waits up to timeout_secs then synthesizes {"error":"client_tool_timeout"}.

parameters.name: connectors
parameters.description: Display names from list_available_connectors, the user, or an auth-error (e.g. "Linear"). Not UUIDs. At most 3.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Short reason shown on the connect card, in the user's terms, explaining why these connectors are needed.

tools.name: get_device_location
tools.description:
Request a fresh device location from the client. If a Location line in the developer prompt already gives enough precision for the task, do not call this.
Success is a JSON object with any subset of: latitude, longitude, accuracy_m, city, region, postal_code, country, formatted_address, source ("gps", "ip", or "user"). On denial or failure: {"error": "permission_denied"|"unavailable"|"user_cancelled"}.
The server waits up to timeout_secs then synthesizes {"error": "client_tool_timeout"}.

parameters.name: details
parameters.description: Fields to include when available. Omit or use [] for coordinates only (latitude, longitude, accuracy_m). address means formatted_address. The client may return a subset and should not add unlisted fields, except source.

parameters.name: importance
parameters.description: How much this turn depends on a fresh device location. Omit for optional. optional = do not block; the client may return nothing. recommended = a non-blocking card / soft prompt is ok. required = a blocking OS permission prompt is ok.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user one or more clarifying questions and wait for their answer before continuing. Use when only the user can provide the information you need to proceed.

parameters.name: questions
parameters.description: One or more questions to ask the user.
